papers.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
papers.abstract: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nystr\"om trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

papers.title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Tur\'an numbers and beyond
papers.abstract: The Hadwiger-Debrunner number $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)$ is defined as the maximum piercing number over all finite families of compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ in which among every $p$ sets, some $q$ have non-empty intersection. We develop three complementary constructions that improve lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. For any fixed $q>d\ge 2$, a randomly sparsified family of hyperplanes, analyzed using hypergraph containers, yields $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)\ge p^{(d+q-2)/(q-1)+o(1)}$ as $p\rightarrow\infty$. To deduce further bounds, we establish a transfer argument from upper bounds on the sizes of sufficiently general-positioned subsets of high-dimensional integer grids to lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. Two methodologies are adopted to derive the former: one connects rainbow Tur\'an theory and general-positioned grid sets, and the other uses full spark linear reduction of tuples with bounded-size preimages. As a combinatorial ingredient, we describe the rainbow Tur\'an behavior under suspension operations, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: A simple proof of the characterization of $\ell_\infty^n$ by norm-one projections and a stability estimate
papers.abstract: We give a short and elementary proof of a classical fact that an $n$-dimensional real or complex normed space with the absolute projection constant equal to one is linearly isometric to $\ell_\infty^n$. The proof uses only finite-dimensional convexity and linear algebra, with no infinite-dimensional ingredients. The same approach yields a quantitative stability estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when the absolute projection constant is at most $1+\varepsilon$. This improves Zippin's estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{8}}$ in each fixed dimension as $\varepsilon \to 0$. The real and complex cases are treated by the same arguments.

papers.title: A generic $p$-Wasserstein space is isometrically rigid
papers.abstract: We prove for any parameter $p \geq 1$ that the $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ of a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X)$ is isometrically rigid, that is, its isometries are precisely the push-forwards of the isometries of $(X,d_X).$ We also study the question whether the isometry class of a $p$-Wasserstein space completely determines the isometry class of the underlying space. We prove for any $p\geq 1$ that for a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X),$ its $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ is isometric to another $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(Y,d_Y)$ if and only if $(Y,d_Y)$ is isometric to $(X,d_X).$ En route we prove that a stronger property, which we call the Dirac preservation property, is also generic.

papers.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
papers.abstract: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.

papers.title: On perturbations that preserve the connectivity properties in tree percolations
papers.abstract: We consider a general bond percolation on an infinite locally finite tree, where the edge retention probabilities $p_e$ are replaced by $\min\{1,q_{|e|}p_e\}$, where $\{q_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of positive perturbation factors and $|e|$ denotes the distance between the edge $e$ and the root. If the original percolation model admits infinite clusters, it is of interest to investigate under which perturbations $0<q_n\le 1$ this connectivity property is preserved. Conversely, if the original percolation does not admit infinite clusters, we are led to study the stability of such a property under perturbations satisfying $q_n\ge 1$. In both cases, under minimal assumptions on the original model, we show that the percolative behaviour is stable against certain quantitative non-trivial perturbations. We also discuss an application of our results to the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture for Cantor sets.

papers.title: Mutually touching cylinders: Littlewood's seven, and at most ten in general
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that at most seven congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can touch pairwise. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968. For cylinders of arbitrary radii we prove the upper bound ten. Whether ten can be attained remains open.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

papers.title: Tangent lengths and invariants of Poncelet polygons between two circles
papers.abstract: A polygon inscribed in one circle and circumscribed about another moves in a one-parameter family, by Poncelet's porism. We study this family through the tangent lengths from the vertices to the inner circle and find a number of quantities that remain constant during the motion. For example, the sum of the fourth powers of the distances from the circumcenter to the points of contact, plus twice the squared area, is constant. We also obtain a version of Euler's formula for $n$-gons, extend a problem on bicentric hexagons from Kvant, and find a second quadratic invariant that goes along with the classical theorem of Weill. The basic invariants have elementary proofs; for the main ones we give two proofs, one of them without derivatives. Reciprocation at a limiting point of the two circles turns these results into statements about billiards in ellipses, and gives short proofs of theorems of Akopyan, Schwartz and Tabachnikov and of Bialy and Tabachnikov. Using the elliptic curve of the family, we show that the area determines the polygon up to a reflection, find the polygons of largest and smallest area, which proves two conjectures of Cie\'slak and Mozgawa, and find all points for which the product of the distances to the vertices is constant.

papers.title: Iterated Steiner symmetrization of convex bodies always converges in shape
papers.abstract: We prove that every sequence of iterated Steiner symmetrals of a convex body converges in shape. That is, every such sequence can be corrected by a sequence of rotations to achieve convergence in Hausdorff distance. Moreover, for a fixed corresponding family of subspaces, the same rotations can be used for every initial convex body, and their successive increments can be chosen to be square-summable.

papers.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. The proof combines explicit bounds on the number of control arcs, local cost inequalities and rigorous finite verification of the remaining switching types.

papers.title: Regularity of Gaussian processes, metric entropy and the Wills functional
papers.abstract: We establish exact relations between three quantities: the growth of the Gaussian Wills functional under dilations, the small-scale metric entropy of the index set, and the critical H\"older exponent of the associated isonormal Gaussian process. For every compact Gaussian-bounded set $T$, the Wills growth exponent $\rho(T)$, the entropy exponent $\eta(T)$, and the critical H\"older exponent $\alpha_H(T)$ satisfy \[ \eta(T)=\frac{2\rho(T)}{2-\rho(T)}, \qquad \alpha_H(T) =1-\frac{\eta(T)}{2} =\frac{2-2\rho(T)}{2-\rho(T)}. \] Thus any one of these parameters determines the other two. Our main tools are a Wills-functional analogue of Sudakov's minoration and a complementary upper bound for $W(rT)$ in terms of local Gaussian widths.

papers.title: Infinite Euclidean Distance Discriminants
papers.abstract: We study infinite Euclidean distance discriminants of algebraic varieties, defined as the loci of data points whose fibers under the second projection from the Euclidean distance correspondence are positive-dimensional. In particular, these discriminants contain all data points with infinitely many critical points for the nearest-point problem. We present computer code that computes the infinite Euclidean distance discriminant, and use it to present numerous varieties with nonempty such discriminants. Moreover, we prove that for any data point, the fiber under the second projection is contained in a finite union of hyperspheres centered at that point. For curves, we include a complete characterization; their infinite Euclidean distance discriminants turn out to be affine linear spaces. Finally, we introduce and characterize skew-tube surfaces in three-dimensional space. By construction, these have a one-dimensional infinite Euclidean distance discriminant. We further demonstrate that many skew-tubes have significantly lower Euclidean distance degrees than generic surfaces of the same degree.

papers.title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
papers.abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Using two results from Fourier's preprint, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these values of $k$. The second version of Fourier's preprint gives an independent proof of this statement. For $k=1$, the equality statement is false: the polytopes $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have the same number of edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. Together with Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. Our results are formalized in Lean 4, with one result of Fourier's preprint and three published results taken as hypotheses.

papers.title: The geometry of magnitude for finite metric spaces
papers.abstract: The main result of this article is a geometric interpretation of magnitude, a real-valued invariant of metric spaces. We introduce a Euclidean embedding of a (suitable) finite metric space $X$ such that the magnitude of $X$ can be expressed in terms of the `circumradius' of its embedding $S$. The circumradius is the radius of the unique sphere that goes through $S$. We give three applications: First, we describe the asymptotic behaviour of the magnitude of $tX$ as $t\rightarrow \infty$, in terms of the circumradius. Second, we develop a matrix theory for magnitude that leads to explicit relations between the magnitude of $X$ and the magnitude of its subspaces. Third, we identify a new regime in the limiting behaviour of $tX$, and use this to show submodularity-type results for magnitude as a function on subspaces.
